notes.6: Question 6 was answered correctly by 40 per cent who chose option C . 7 per cent chose option A , 45 per cent chose option B and 7 per cent chose option D . 1 per cent did not answer the question. A tax on a good would increase the cost of the good and shift the supply curve. Those candidates who chose option B recognised that demand would be likely to fall but as this fall was because of the rise in the price it would be shown on the diagram by a movement along the demand curve and not by a shift in the demand curve to D 3.
notes.8: Question 8 was answered correctly by 35 per cent who chose option B . 39 per cent chose option A , 13 per cent chose option C and 13 per cent chose option D . Those candidates who chose option A may well have not noticed that the question asked what was not a market failure. Option A , external costs of production, is classified as a market failure. Similarly, over-consumption of de-merit goods and under-consumption of merit goods cause a misallocation of resources and are market failures. The only option that is not a market failure is B .
notes.16: Question 16 was answered correctly by 37 per cent who chose option C . 41 per cent chose option A , 17 per cent chose option B and 5 per cent chose option D . A government budget has both revenue and expenditure. Government revenue comes partly from taxation so the correct answer is indirect tax revenue.
